turns.question: I'm starting to think seriously about retiring but I honestly don't know where to begin. What should I be thinking about?
turns.answer:
Start with your planned withdrawal date, your age and service at that date, and which annuity choices under Article 11 you want compared. Your record places you in Article 11; tell me if that is not right.

- Section 11-134 provides several retirement annuity choices for employees with at least 20 years of service. Some choices use the highest average annual salary for 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years, while another uses 5 consecutive years. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- Because you are under age 60, the applicable choice may include a reduction for each month or fractional part of a month that the annuity begins before age 60. Some provisions remove that reduction when the service requirement is met. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- Section 11-134 also provides elections “in lieu of” other employee annuities. The Code therefore requires a comparison of the choices that reach you; the figure cannot be worked out here without knowing the retirement date and the option you choose. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- The early-retirement incentive provisions are tied to elections and withdrawal dates in 1998 or 2004. They do not reach a retirement decision being made now. [40 ILCS 5/11-133.2; 40 ILCS 5/11-133.3]

cases.name: A survivor question that uses none of the survivor vocabulary

turns.question: My wife is worried about what happens to her if something happens to me. What would she get?
turns.answer:
If you die while still in service, your eligible spouse may receive an annuity under Article 11. The provision that applies provides an annuity equal to 50% of the minimum formula annuity earned and accrued to your credit at the date of death. It is not reduced because of your age or your spouse’s age. [40 ILCS 5/11-145.1(k)]

Your record shows 21.5 years of service, which meets the required 10 years of service. Your marriage must also have been in effect for at least 10 full years. I would need the date of your death in service, confirmation that the death occurred while you were in service, and the length of your marriage in full years. The date and in-service status determine whether this provision applies; the marriage length determines whether your wife is eligible.

Subsections (a) and (b) are superseded here because subsection (k) applies “in lieu of any other annuity” under Article 11. [40 ILCS 5/11-145.1(k)]

This does not cover tax treatment or life-insurance benefits; the IRS handles taxes, and your fund or employer’s HR office handles insurance.

cases.name: Half inside the Code and half outside it

turns.question: Does any of this get taxed, and do I still get health insurance?
turns.answer:
The Pension Code does not decide whether your pension is taxable or whether you keep health insurance after retirement.

For health benefits, the Code allows the Board to provide regulations under which an annuitant or pensioner may assign all or part of an annuity or disability benefit to pay premiums for hospital or medical insurance for you, your spouse, and your children. The Board may end that assignment option. [40 ILCS 5/11-223.1] The Code also provides payments toward certain City health care plans for eligible city annuitants, but only through December 31, 2016, or until the City no longer provides the plan, whichever comes first. [40 ILCS 5/11-160.1]

Tax treatment belongs to the IRS, and your continuing health-insurance eligibility and coverage terms belong to the Fund and your employer's HR or benefits office.
